headline: Thursday Night Football: Buccaneers and Falcons clash for NFC South supremacy
whyCareReason: Baker Mayfield and Kirk Cousins meet under the prime-time lights in Atlanta with first place in the division on the line and two high-powered offenses in form.
teaser: Tampa Bay enters 3-1 after blowing out Philadelphia, while Atlanta sits 2-2 following a buzzer-beating divisional triumph over New Orleans.
story:
Why this one matters: Divisional games in October are where division races are won or lost. On Thursday night at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Atlanta Falcons meet with the outright lead in the NFC South hanging in the balance.

Baker Mayfield has completely revitalized his career in Tampa Bay. Through four weeks, Mayfield leads the NFC with eight touchdown passes against only two interceptions, carrying a sparkling 106.9 passer rating. Coming off a 33-16 demolition of the Philadelphia Eagles in which he dissected the secondary for 347 yards, Mayfield enters Atlanta with supreme confidence and an embarrassment of riches in Mike Evans and Chris Godwin.

For Kirk Cousins and the Falcons, Thursday presents an immediate litmus test. Atlanta averted an early-season crisis on Sunday when Younghoe Koo drilled a 58-yard field goal with two ticks remaining to sink the Saints 26-24. But Raheem Morris knows that field goals will not be enough against Tampa's potent attack. The Falcons need a signature performance from Bijan Robinson on the ground and sharp decision-making from Cousins to seize control of the South.
stakes: First place in the NFC South: a Tampa Bay victory pushes the Bucs to 4-1 with two divisional wins, while an Atlanta triumph pulls both teams level at 3-2.
rivalryAngle: The all-time head-to-head series between these NFC South rivals stands dead even at 30-30, with four of the last five meetings decided by one possession.
